jobs.title: Account Executive (Hotels)
jobs.description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: The Airbnb Hotels team is a fun, fast-growing group leading Airbnb’s expansion into the hotel sector. Operating with an entrepreneurial spirit, this team combines the simplicity, product excellence, and guest-centered ethos that define Airbnb. This team’s mission is to deliver the smoothest, most intuitive hotel booking experience for guests, while helping independent, boutique hotels easily drive incremental bookings so they can focus on delivering the best hospitality. The ultimate aim is to help more people discover high-quality hotels, creating value for guests and our hotel partners. The Difference You Will Make As an Account Executive, you will be responsible for converting leads into net‑new supply to support new-market launches and at pace to hit quarterly goals. Working the full sales funnel, you will proactively turn cold leads into warm sales opportunities helping to build the Hotels category’s market presence in the process through collaboration with other teams. This includes partnering, strategizing, and running daily operations directly with independent, boutique hotels, and ensuring that Airbnb sources  the best hotel inventory available to our guests. A Typical Day Meet and exceed KPIs by owning the performance and success of assigned region Prospect new potential hotels through external research, networking, and use of Airbnb tools Securing new hotels involves targeted sales strategies and negotiating and closing the deals Develops acquisition strategies and scalable, localised supply strategies for established and emerging markets Expertly position and communicate Airbnb’s value proposition to new partners via phone, email, and in-person Add net new hotels by qualifying and moving leads through the funnel as quickly as possible, achieving defined quarterly goals Find supply in and launch new markets: Own market launches including supporting lead generation and coordinating cross functionally Support hotel onboarding as needed from won sales opportunities Effectively promote and build strong relationships with hotels by demonstrating comprehensive knowledge of our platforms and confidently pitching their value Your Expertise 6+ years of professional experience, preferably in a fast growing startup tech or hospitality company working in sales and/or account management Previous hospitality experience is a plus Proficiency in both English and Spanish is a must! Portuguese is a plus.  CRM required; Proficiency in Salesforce, Gong and other scalable AI Sales prospecting tools is a plus. The ability to get things done with constantly changing priorities, projects and deadlines Excellent communication, organizational, and analytical skills, detail-oriented but moves fast Ability to establish strong relationships with and influence partners  Capacity to balance day-to-day responsibilities with longer-term strategic execution You’re a quick learner and you’re fearless about doing whatever it takes to get the job done, even if it means making mistakes along the way Able to travel up to 25-30% of the time Passion for Airbnb and travel How We’ll Take Care of You: Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for variable incentive pay, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits. The On-Target Earnings (“OTE”) range for this role is €63,000 to €73,000 gross per year, which includes a split of 80% (base pay) / 20% (variable incentive). Of this OTE amount, the annual gross base salary range is €50,400 to €58,400.  The OTE reflected on this job posting is the target cash compensation a candidate could earn in a year if they achieve 100% of their performance or sales goals. The variable incentive is not guaranteed and is governed by the terms of Airbnb’s Hotels Variable Compensation Plan (the “Plan”). The actual payouts depend on performance against targets set under the “Plan” and may be higher or lower than the range listed on this job posting.  Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging: Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.   Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role. A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @ airbnb.com or @ ext.airbnb.com email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing.  We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. jobs.title: Business Operations and Growth Lead
jobs.description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join:  The Chief Business Officer organization plays a pivotal role in driving the company’s growth and expansion efforts worldwide. Our teammates work on commercializing Airbnb’s new and existing businesses, helping Airbnb expand beyond its core offering as a place to stay. This includes recruiting and developing Airbnb’s global supply of high-quality stays, Experiences, and Services, and executing Airbnb’s global strategy in the market. With a focus on business strategy, quality supply and international expansion, the team is leading the way for Airbnb’s continued growth and success in its next chapter.  The Global Markets Team, which sits within CBO, ensures that Airbnb is locally relevant and serves the needs of our global hosts and guests, helping regions more efficiently plan and execute growth strategies across supply, demand, and other surfaces in a way that will resonate with our communities.  The Difference You Will Make :  You will work closely with the cross-functional leaders and teams, and play a key role in scaling our community growth and optimization-focused programs. The successful candidate will report to the Director, Programs and Business Operations.  A Typical Day:  Align all functions  to achieve Americas’s regional business objectives in partnership with the Director, Regional Business Operations and Growth. Own the conception, execution, and measurement of cross-functional initiatives end-to-end. Concretely, this means defining a crisp problem statement, articulating the ideal solution to that problem, identifying key dependencies blocking that solution, and then working with cross-functional stakeholders to achieve the solution. These initiatives will span across the demand, supply, and regulatory surfaces of the business.  Drive regular business operation meetings and initiate meaningful conversations - leading weekly meetings with cross-functional project teams (field & online operations, marketing, product, legal) to ensure key initiatives are on track. Use all available data sources and tools, internal and external, to analyze macro and micro trends, and present analysis, insights, and actionable plans to Airbnb country and regional leadership team to drive key business decisions.  Assist the Regional Director and Regional BizOps Director in owning the performance narrative for key metrics and deliver the story to senior leaders in a concise and clear manner in weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews Your Expertise:  Qualified candidates will ideally have a minimum of 10+ years of work experience, preferably with combined exposure to data-modeling, business analytics, and project management in a dynamic entrepreneurial environment.  A proven bias to action and ability to own a project from conception through to post-mortem. Ability to work in a world of uncertainty and ambiguity - to create clarity from chaos. jobs.description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. The community you will join: Airbnb's mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. We're seeking a NextStay Fellow to help pursue that mission as a hands-on Technical Program Manager (TPM) in our engineering organization. The NextStay Fellowship is a launchpad: you'll join with a strong program management foundation and grow into the full scope and ambiguity of the role, supported by experienced TPMs and engineering partners invested in your success.   A typical day: Lead execution of a project with a defined scope and approach, turning direction from your manager or senior TPMs into a concrete, realistic plan built around known constraints. Break work into trackable pieces and use input and output metrics to monitor progress, surfacing slippage before it becomes a problem. Lead alignment of the project team and hold contributors accountable to deliverables and milestones, while anticipating the next set of work. Consult team members or leaders to identify risks and mitigation options; track and manage risks you've already identified through to resolution. Communicate the project's vision and success criteria clearly to your project team and stakeholders, and re-evaluate strategy with guidance from leadership on when to pivot versus stay the course. Ask the right questions to surface potential technical gaps, working collaboratively with engineers and applying a working understanding of sound technical principles. Working under the guidance of senior TPMs, you'll hold the program accountable to deliverables while managing scope, schedule, and quality trade-offs, re-planning proactively as conditions change and escalating the decisions that carry real business risk. Core manager competencies include: Scope Management – Partners with the team to define boundaries and milestones against program objectives, enabling informed trade-off conversations and preventing scope creep across teams. Schedule Management – Breaks work into sized, sequenced pieces with clear dependencies, builds a schedule with technical partners, and communicates changes as they arise. Quality – Establishes the expected level of quality during planning and treats it as a fixed constraint alongside schedule and scope. Risk Identification – Surfaces upstream and downstream dependencies and risks early, analyzing them within the context of the overall plan. jobs.title: Partenaire principal de planification, Contenu
jobs.description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. La communauté à laquelle vous vous joindrez Vous deviendrez un membre clé de l’équipe de planification du soutien à la communauté des Opérations mondiales. Cette équipe pilote le processus de planification de la feuille de route, de bout en bout, pour le soutien à la communauté d’Airbnb. Elle veille à ce que les initiatives et les programmes soient priorisés en fonction de notre stratégie globale et de notre engagement à offrir une expérience client exceptionnelle. Nous sommes une équipe mondiale experte en planification stratégique, en gestion des parties prenantes, en collaboration interfonctionnelle et en efficacité organisationnelle. La différence que vous ferez À titre de partenaire principal de planification, Contenu, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel dans la réussite et la satisfaction de notre clientèle grâce à une gestion des relations rigoureuse et à une collaboration stratégique. Vous soutiendrez un ou plusieurs domaines de produits et serez la personne-ressource principale des gestionnaires de contenu, des rédacteurs et rédactrices ainsi que des stratèges de ces domaines. Vous assurerez la planification et la coordination de bout en bout de chaque lancement qui a une incidence sur le contenu du soutien à la communauté. Vous veillerez à ce que la communication soit claire, que les objectifs soient harmonisés et que le contenu soit livré à temps et avec un haut niveau de qualité au moment du lancement. Vous repérerez de façon proactive les occasions d’ajouter de la valeur tout en vous attaquant aux difficultés potentielles, avec toujours en tête d’obtenir des résultats mesurables pour notre clientèle et pour l’entreprise. Votre capacité à établir des relations de confiance avec les partenaires du contenu, du produit, de l’ingénierie, du marketing et des affaires juridiques, alliée à votre esprit stratégique et à votre rigueur d’exécution, contribuera au bon déroulement des lancements ainsi qu’à la réussite de notre clientèle et de l’organisation. Une journée type Établir un dialogue proactif avec les partenaires et les parties prenantes interfonctionnels : suivis réguliers, communication des échéanciers de planification et des jalons à venir, séances de rétroaction. Le but est de bâtir la confiance et de s’assurer de l’harmonisation avec leurs buts et objectifs. Déterminer à l’avance toutes les personnes responsables de chaque lancement : le rédacteur ou la rédactrice et le ou la stratège du contenu touché; les personnes chargées d’approuver le contenu pour le marketing, les affaires juridiques et l’expertise technique; les partenaires de localisation; et les partenaires interfonctionnels, comme la taxonomie, la formation, le centre de ressources, Biztech et les autres gestionnaires de projet dont les travaux sont liés. Élaborer le calendrier du contenu et le communiquer à toutes les personnes qui demandent du contenu et à celles qui l’approuvent. Pour ce faire, recueillir les dates d’indisponibilité des personnes chargées d’approuver et prévoir du temps pour les audits de contenu, la rédaction, la vérification de l’exactitude technique, la révision par le marketing, la révision juridique et la localisation, ainsi qu’une marge pour les imprévus. Planifier et animer la série de réunions de chaque lancement : la séance de collecte d’information sur le lancement avec les équipes du produit, de l’ingénierie et de la préparation au lancement; les séances d’audit de contenu; une réunion préalable au lancement avec le marketing; une réunion hebdomadaire récurrente sur l’état du lancement avec l’équipe de contenu et les experts techniques; et, le jour du lancement, une réunion « Mission Control » et un canal Slack. Collaborer avec les stratèges lors des audits de contenu pour repérer tout le contenu touché, en hiérarchiser les répercussions (P1 : jour du lancement; P2 : suivis à court terme; P3 : tous les autres éléments), s’assurer qu’un billet est ouvert pour chaque article touché et signaler le contenu lié à l’interface utilisateur ainsi que les exigences de localisation. Préparer et envoyer chaque semaine un compte rendu de l’état d’avancement aux gestionnaires de contenu et aux personnes responsables du contenu, incluant la liste des articles touchés et leur état P1/P2/P3, afin que les risques (calendrier des audits, approbations en retard, changements de date de lancement) soient visibles rapidement. Anticiper les risques et les problèmes, et élaborer de façon proactive des stratégies d’atténuation (aller au-delà du simple suivi de l’état d’avancement et mener les problèmes jusqu’à leur résolution). Maintenir un processus pour repérer les demandes de contenu tardives et les signaler comme étant « à risque ». Envoyer régulièrement des rappels aux personnes ayant des responsabilités liées au lancement et, lorsque les personnes chargées d’approuver ne répondent pas en mode asynchrone, planifier des rencontres d’approbation en direct avec le marketing, l’ingénierie, les affaires juridiques et d’autres intervenants. Préparer des communications interfonctionnelles à l’intention des équipes partenaires touchées par notre travail, comme la localisation, Biztech, la gestion des connaissances et la formation. Coordonner en temps réel la mise en ligne le jour du lancement, une fois le feu vert donné par l’équipe de préparation au lancement, afin que l’équipe de contenu sache qu’elle peut publier en toute sécurité. Participer aux réunions de lancement, aux séances de coordination en temps réel et aux séances du centre de contact organisées par d’autres équipes afin d’être la voix de l’équipe de contenu, de faire le point, de répondre aux questions et de tenir l’équipe de contenu informée des problèmes émergents. jobs.title: Senior Accountant, Consolidations
jobs.description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join:  We are the Consolidations & Intercompany team within Accounting & Reporting. We consolidate Airbnb's financial results across its global legal entities and manage the intercompany activity that connects them, so the books stay accurate, compliant with US GAAP, and closed on time. You will work across Finance, partnering with Treasury, Tax, and Finance Systems on funding, transfer pricing, and process optimization. The Difference You Will Make: As Senior Accountant, Consolidations, you will support the day-to-day and key intercompany and consolidations accounting activities, particularly during month-end close, where success means hitting each business day milestone. You will serve as a resource on intercompany topics across the wider Finance organization, including support for internal and external audit requests. You will challenge how things are done today and carry better ways of working through to implementation, in our processes and in the ones we share with cross-functional partners. A Typical Day:  Own your assigned close areas from start to finish, preparing and posting monthly intercompany and consolidation journal entries and reconciliations by the close milestone dates, including global funding and settlements, ad hoc cash transfers, recharges, and eliminations like intercompany profit. Prepare and post journal entries for foreign currency transactions, redenominations, and translation adjustments. Work with Treasury on cash pool and intercompany funding accounting, including settlements with FX, accrued and capitalized interest, and reconciliations. Work with Treasury, Tax, and other Controlling teams to clear intercompany imbalances and close blockers, raising risks early with a proposed fix, and serve as a resource on intercompany topics such as consolidation and eliminations (ASC 810), foreign currency, and capital transactions. Keep documentation, workpapers, and SOPs current so the work is repeatable and audit-ready, and respond to internal, external, and statutory audit requests. Cut manual work out of the close. jobs.title: Senior Enablement Manager - API

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join The Enterprise Operations organization is instrumental in powering Airbnb's growth and expansion at a global scale. Through AI- and people-powered operations, this team maximizes the effectiveness, utilization, and impact of our supply, ensuring hosts and guests can seamlessly connect. The Supply Enablement & Activation team is a horizontal Center of Excellence within Enterprise Operations, serving as a strategic partner to global field and vendor teams by driving standardized strategy, tools, and best practices at scale. We turn our supply strategy into repeatable, scalable, best in class enablement deliverables – collateral, training, tools & workflows, and comms/change management -- for our sales & operator teams across each line of business: Homes, Hotels, Experiences & Services. This role supports the API team, which sits at the heart of Airbnb's Supply strategy, managing the connectivity partners — property management software providers, channel managers, and distribution platforms — that power a significant share of our global inventory. These partnerships unlock access to millions of listings and directly shape the quality and reliability of the host and guest experience. At the center of this work are our Connectivity Partner Managers, who own Airbnb's relationships with these third-party technology providers — PMS (Property Management System), channel manager, and revenue management tool vendors that hosts and property managers use to sync listings, calendars, pricing, and reservations with Airbnb. Connectivity Partner Managers are the primary point of contact for these partners: they ensure integrations meet Airbnb's connectivity standards, resolve sync and data issues, onboard new partners, negotiate partnership terms, drive adoption of Airbnb's APIs among software vendors, and work with Product and Engineering to prioritize roadmap improvements based on partner feedback. The Difference You Will Make We're looking for a seasoned Senior Enablement Manager to build and own end-to-end enablement for Airbnb's API team and Connectivity Partner Managers across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. This is a newly approved, full-time role created to close a resourcing gap: enablement support for API has historically been covered informally and part-time, and this role will stand up a sustainable, scalable enablement function from the ground up. The core of this role is to enable our Connectivity Partner Managers to do their jobs more effectively and drive tangible impact. Connectivity Partner Managers own the full relationship with PMS, channel manager, and revenue management tool partners — from onboarding and integration standards to sync/data issue resolution, contract negotiation, API adoption, and roadmap prioritization with Product and Engineering. You will build the onboarding curriculum, training, playbooks, and certifications that ramp new Connectivity Partner Managers; keep them current on product launches, API versions, and roadmap changes; and equip them with the narratives, tools, and processes they need to manage partner relationships and escalations with confidence. This is a highly cross-functional, more technical role than a typical field-enablement position — it requires deep, ongoing engagement with the Product roadmap and with Connectivity Partner Managers themselves, not a copy-paste of a direct-sales enablement playbook. You will own onboarding, training, and continuous development for teams supporting API partners; drive consistent acquisition, growth, and retention of high-quality supply; and localize global enablement programs for regional relevance. You'll partner cross-functionally to collect and share feedback, and use enablement tools and insights to continuously improve outcomes. and training for Connectivity Partner Managers so they are fully equipped with managing partners effectively and shaping their behaviour  Revive and scale partner-facing enablement channels, including jobs.title: Abuse Investigator
jobs.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Abuse Operations is the front-line incident response and remediation function handling active product abuse and fraud impacting Stripe and its merchants. This multi-disciplinary group, spanning Incident Managers, Investigators, Forward Deployed Security Engineers, and Data Scientists, neutralizes active attacks, gathers requirements for operational tooling, and leads incidents. The team  works directly with impacted merchants to resolve technical incidents and policy abuse rapidly. Operating primarily across Eastern, Pacific and Western European time zones, these team members regularly coordinate with global stakeholders across the world. What you’ll do You'll play a critical role in safeguarding our financial ecosystem by investigating high-risk accounts and identifying complex patterns of fraud during incidents. You will lead incident response for product abuse and fraud events, conducting deep-dive analyses to identify root causes. By collaborating cross-functionally, you will drive improvements that enhance our fraud detection and prevention strategies at scale. Your expertise will be essential in automating response processes through agentic approaches, allowing us to safeguard merchants and neutralize threats with speed and precision. Responsibilities Investigate, mitigate, and remediate urgent fraud incidents (e.g., ATO, card testing), utilizing FT3-mapped detection and signals enrichment to reduce uncertainty and accelerate response. As part of incidents, analyze high-risk accounts to identify fraudulent merchants, card testing, account takeovers, and other fraud vectors, classifying them using FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0) to standardize threat intelligence. Lead incident root cause analyses to identify gaps in current systems and strategies, leveraging the FT3 framework, data-driven model to drive enhancements and process improvements for emerging fraud risks. Streamline incident response capabilities, ensuring the tooling and processes are clear, accurate and efficient Work cross-functionally with security, fraud and data science teams to build agentic solutions for responding to abuse incidents at scale Effectively communicate cross-functionally with legal and policy teams to assess and mitigate risks, while demonstrating strong problem-solving under pressure. Collaborate effectively with teammates, leading projects, mentoring others, and developing and championing quality standards within the team Who you are We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 3+ years of experience conducting incident response in security, product abuse or trust domains 3+ years experience analyzing large data sets to solve problems and/or building models with a behavioral approach to fraud detection B.S. or M.S. Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience Expert knowledge of Python and SQL, and familiarity with other programming languages Existing experience with log analysis (e.g. first or third party applications, system / data access, event logs), network security, digital forensics, and incident response investigations Ability to communicate results clearly and focus on impact Ability to think creatively and holistically about reducing risk in a complex environment Preferred qualifications An adversarial mindset, understanding the goals, behaviors, and TTPs of threat actors. Experience with engineering, data processing and analysis tools (e.g. Databricks, Trino, etc.) Familiarity with common open-source frameworks for big data processing and/or data science (PySpark, Pandas, Sci-kit Learn, etc.) Experience with tactical threat intelligence and/or hunting for sophisticated threat actors in an enterprise environment Ability to proactively challenge the status quo by leveraging data and taking a user-centric approach to address complex product integrity challenges

jobs.title: Account Executive, Product - Buy Now Pay Later (AUNZ)
jobs.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. About the team Payments Product Sales is a team of deep functional and technical specialists who lead and advise on opportunities for some of the most strategically important products in Stripe’s portfolio. We work alongside Stripe’s Core Sales and Customer Success teams to help users adopt products that improve their payment experiences, support international growth, and create new sources of revenue. We are hiring an Account Executive, Product - Buy Now Pay Later to grow adoption of Klarna and Affirm among Stripe users across APAC. Based in Australia, this role will have an initial emphasis on Australia and other priority APAC markets. The Account Executive will primarily lead customer-facing sales motions and will also work with Stripe’s Partnerships team and our BNPL partners on strategic three-party opportunities. What you’ll do As an Account Executive, Product focused on Buy Now Pay Later, you will be a quota-carrying product-sales overlay responsible for growing adoption and payment volume across new and existing Stripe users. You will partner closely with Core Account Executives and Customer Success Managers throughout the sales cycle—from identifying and qualifying opportunities through commercial negotiation, technical validation, implementation, activation, and expansion. You will develop deep expertise in Klarna, Affirm, the BNPL market, and the needs of users operating across APAC. You will lead business and technical conversations with stakeholders ranging from product and engineering teams to C-level executives, helping users understand how BNPL can support their customer experience and growth objectives. For strategic opportunities, you will coordinate across the user, Stripe, and the BNPL provider to align commercial terms, implementation plans, and launch requirements. You are an adept salesperson who can build value in complex and competitive situations. You are comfortable navigating technical product discussions, complex customer organizations, and multi-party negotiations. You are equally effective with users and internal stakeholders, and you enjoy turning early customer signals into repeatable go-to-market motions. Responsibilities Deliver against an individual quota by driving adoption and payment volume for Klarna, Affirm and new potential BNPL partners across new and existing Stripe users in APAC. Partner with Core Account Executives and Customer Success Managers to identify, qualify, develop, and close high-potential BNPL opportunities. Build territory and account strategies that reflect user needs and payment preferences across Australia and other priority APAC markets. Lead discovery with business, product, finance, and technical stakeholders and articulate a clear value proposition for BNPL adoption. Develop customer-specific business cases that connect BNPL to user growth, customer experience, conversion, and global expansion objectives. Navigate complex sales cycles and lead negotiations involving users, Stripe, and BNPL partners, working closely with Partnerships on commercial structure and partner alignment. Coordinate with Solutions Architecture, Product, Engineering, and Post-Sales teams to translate user requirements into viable solutions and help users progress from decision to implementation and activation. Maintain senior relationships with users and develop productive working relationships with Klarna, Affirm and new potential BNPL partners. Monitor adoption and payment volume after launch, identify expansion opportunities, and work with account teams to address barriers to growth. Serve as an internal and customer-facing BNPL expert, creating enablement and repeatable sales plays that improve the effectiveness of Stripe’s broader field organization. Synthesize market intelligence and user feedback for Product, Engineering, Partnerships, and Marketing to help inform product and go-to-market priorities. Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 5+ years of experience in sales, business development, partnerships, or a closely related commercial role at a technology company, with a track record of strong performance against goals. Experience leading complex B2B sales cycles involving multiple business, commercial, and technical stakeholders. Ability to understand technical product requirements and translate them into clear customer outcomes and commercially viable solutions. Strong executive presence and the ability to communicate effectively with product and engineering teams, operational leaders, and C-level executives. Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships and influence cross-functional teams without direct authority. Experience developing business cases and negotiating bespoke or multi-party commercial agreements. A self-starting, highly organized approach and the ability to deliver results in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment. Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and analytical skills. Willingness to travel approximately 10% of the time for user meetings, team events, sales kickoffs, and occasional international business needs. Preferred qualifications Experience in payments, Buy Now Pay Later, alternative payment methods, ecommerce, or financial technology. Knowledge of the APAC payments landscape, particularly Australia and other priority markets in the region. Experience working in a product-sales overlay model alongside account executives, customer success teams, or technical sellers. Experience managing strategic partner relationships or three-party sales motions. Familiarity with product-led integrations and the commercial and technical considerations involved in launching a new payment method. jobs.title: Account Executive, Product Sales - Open Issuance
jobs.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe builds financial infrastructure for businesses—from ambitious startups to global enterprises. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we’re building the tools that help businesses participate in and grow the global economy. About the team Stripe’s Crypto team is building financial infrastructure for a world where money moves as easily as information. Across Stripe, Bridge, and Privy, we help businesses build products powered by stablecoins, wallets, and programmable money movement. Open Issuance is central to that opportunity. Built by Bridge, a Stripe company, it enables businesses to launch and manage their own stablecoins. Alongside it, Open Standard—the independent organization behind Open USD (OUSD)—is building a shared stablecoin network with broad distribution and economics designed to benefit the businesses driving adoption.  We’re hiring one of the founding sellers of our Open Issuance go-to-market team. You’ll partner closely with Open Standard and teams across Stripe, Bridge, and Privy on a major strategic bet: challenging the stablecoin duopoly and giving businesses more choice, control, and participation in the economics of digital dollars. This is an opportunity to help build a market—not simply sell into an established one. What you’ll do You’ll own new-business development with high-potential businesses building the next generation of financial products. You’ll help founders, executives, and technical teams understand where stablecoins can create meaningful value, whether through adopting OUSD or launching their own stablecoin with Open Issuance. As a founding seller, you’ll shape the strategy as well as execute it. You’ll identify early customers, develop compelling commercial use cases, close complex deals, and turn those engagements into a repeatable sales motion. You should be equally comfortable opening doors, working through technical and commercial details, and creating structure where no playbook exists. Responsibilities Own a revenue target and the full sales lifecycle, from proactive prospecting and qualification through negotiation, closing, launch, and expansion. Build a net-new pipeline of companies, platforms, fintechs, and other businesses with strong potential to adopt OUSD or Open Issuance. Develop trusted relationships with founders, CEOs, CFOs, and product and engineering leaders, translating complex infrastructure into a clear business case. Partner closely with Open Standard to develop opportunities, coordinate customer engagements, and grow adoption of OUSD. Help customers evaluate opportunities across stablecoin issuance, global money movement, treasury, payouts, and emerging AI and agentic-commerce use cases. Lead technically and commercially complex sales in partnership with Solutions Architecture, Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, and Compliance. Help define the team’s initial customer segments, qualification criteria, positioning, commercial approaches, and operating cadence. Bring structured customer and competitive feedback to Product and Engineering, influencing what we build and how we bring it to market. Turn early wins into repeatable playbooks while remaining hands-on in prospecting, deal execution, and customer launches. Who you are We’re looking for a seller who combines a hunter’s drive with a builder’s mindset. You’re motivated by ambitious targets, but equally interested in understanding how a product works and why a customer should adopt it. You can earn credibility with technical founders, navigate complex organizations, and make progress when the product, market, and sales motion are evolving. If you meet the minimum requirements, we encourage you to apply. Preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a prerequisite. Requirements 5+ years of customer-facing experience in technology, fintech, crypto, payments, or financial infrastructure, with a track record of strong commercial performance. Demonstrated success generating your own pipeline and winning net-new business. Experience leading complex, consultative sales involving multiple stakeholders and customized commercial agreements. Ability to become a trusted advisor to senior business leaders while engaging credibly with product and technical teams. Strong commercial judgment and the ability to connect a customer’s business model, money flows, and product strategy to a compelling solution. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain unfamiliar technical concepts clearly. Comfort operating with autonomy, navigating ambiguity, and building processes rather than relying on an established playbook. A collaborative approach and a willingness to take ownership of the work required to help customers succeed. Preferred qualifications Experience selling to AI-native companies, developer platforms, fintechs, wallets, or crypto-native businesses. Experience with stablecoins, issuance, treasury, cross-border payments, or embedded finance. Experience selling API-based infrastructure or bringing regulated financial products to market. Experience as an early or founding seller who helped build a new product’s go-to-market motion. Familiarity with agentic commerce and the financial infrastructure needs of AI-driven businesses.

About the role We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month. You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI. Key responsibilities Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline. Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments. Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge. Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership. Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting. Serve as the primary contact for external auditors. Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready. Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer. Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close. Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close. Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements. Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326). Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments. Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries. Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence. Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes. Minimum qualifications Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue. Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis. Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger. Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes. Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations. Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits. Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams. Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built. Preferred qualifications Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams. A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA). Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company. Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace). Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models. Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools. Experience with IPO readiness. Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work. You'll operate at the intersection of technical deployment, enablement, and program design. Some days you'll be in the weeds with a customer's IT team debugging a SAML assertion; other days you'll be stepping back to ask how the last ten deployments should change the next hundred. Your systems-thinking approach will directly shape how we activate customers, and your strategic management will ensure every customer achieves meaningful outcomes within their first 90 days. By identifying patterns across activations, you'll build replicable approaches to organizational change while maintaining the agility to customize solutions for each customer's unique transformation journey. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role Anthropic runs one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry, across multiple accelerator families, CPU families, clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites. Capacity Engineering owns the data, tooling, and systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization of that fleet: we partner on supply deals, wire telemetry from day zero, own the canonical capacity data layer, and build the planning and enforcement tools every research and product team relies on. This role sits in the Planning pillar, on the Demand Planning team, and works daily with research engineering, pretraining, inference, compute supply, finance, and external vendors. You own the tranches. The job has two halves that feed each other. Upstream, you take the Demand Planning forecast and turn it into per-tranche requirements — shape, interconnect, region, supporting resources, date — and carry those into sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews so we contract for capacity we can actually use when we need it. Downstream, you own the integrated schedule and system of record for every tranche in flight — from contracted through reserved, ingested, in-cluster, healthy, and occupied — and you drive the owners of each hop to their dates. Take the Demand Planning forecast plus direct input from research, pretraining, and inference planners, and convert it into concrete accelerator, interconnect, region, supporting-resource, and date requirements for each tranche. Represent those in sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews, including which contractual terms actually move delivery dates. Qualify tranches for deliverability before signature. The Capacity Planner signs fit-to-forecast; you sign whether the shape can land schedulable, healthy, and instrumented in that region on that date, with storage, egress, identity in place. Close the delivery loop. Track forecast-versus-delivered on shape, region, and timing for every tranche; publish the variance; and feed it back to Demand Planning and into the next contract. Own the bring-up system of record. Define the canonical contract-to-occupied state machine with explicit entry and exit criteria per stage, and make it a first-class object in the capacity data layer so every downstream tool sees in-flight capacity, not only what has landed. Run a portfolio of bring-ups in parallel — new cloud regions, on-prem sites, neocloud blocks — with one integrated schedule spanning provider milestones, cluster creation, network turn-up, storage readiness, health burn-in, and first-workload landing.  Drive readiness automation: All capacity systems are fully integrated for all new capacity, from contracted through ingested, automated and scaled. jobs.title: Applied AI Architect, Democratic Partnerships
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a member of the Applied AI, Democratic Partnerships team at Anthropic you will provide technical support to the governments of key international allies and civil-sector partners to support democratic resilience. Near-term work focuses on a few priority countries and partners, and will continue to expand with capacity. This role serves Anthropic's mission and public benefit goals.   In collaboration with the Policy, National Security, Product, Research, and Engineering teams, you'll help partners build, integrate, and ship Claude deployments. You will use your excellent communication skills to explain complex topics, including the potential benefits and harms of frontier AI, to technical and non-technical audiences alike. You will also play a critical role in identifying how our AI systems can best serve public interests in frontline democracies, while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards. Responsibilities: Work directly with partner technical teams to build and ship Claude deployments. Guide their setup, architecture, and integration as they build with Claude Code and the Claude API. Build pilots and repeatable workflows that can scale across partner agencies, and support developer and university enablement. Document how to deploy Claude in low-connectivity, multilingual, and security-conscious environments, for reuse across partners. Act as the voice of our partners in frontline democracies and a key collaborator with our Product and Research teams to ensure we deliver the capabilities they need. Travel internationally to partner institutions for technical enablement and building relationships.  Establish a shared vision for creating solutions that enable beneficial and safe AI. Lead the vision, strategy, and execution of innovative solutions that leverage our latest models’ capabilities. Support partner deployments in areas such as education, cyber resiliency and global health. You may be a good fit if you have: 4+ years of experience as a Customer Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Sales Engineer, Solutions Architect, or Cybersecurity Engineer, working with governments, civil-sector organizations, or the public sector Experience shipping software in imperfect conditions, and a practical approach to infrastructure constraints Designed novel and innovative solutions for technical platforms in a developing mission area Comfort working directly with partner technical teams, and motivation to work on deployments where the stakes are civic rather than commercial Strong technical aptitude to partner with engineers and strong proficiency in at least one programming language (Python preferred) Understanding of and experience with LLM fundamentals The ability to navigate and execute amidst ambiguity, and to flex into different domains based on the problem at hand, finding simple, easy-to-understand solutions Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to convey complicated topics in easily understandable terms to a diverse set of external and internal stakeholders, from engineers to senior government officials Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.  For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $240,000 — $315,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage:  Learn about  our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As an Applied AI team member at Anthropic, you will be a pre-sales architect focused on becoming a trusted technical advisor helping large enterprises understand the value of Claude and paint the vision on how they can successfully integrate and deploy Claude into their technology stack. You'll combine your deep technical expertise with customer-facing skills to architect innovative LLM solutions that address complex business challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability. Working closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll guide customers from initial technical discovery through successful deployment. You'll leverage your expertise to help customers understand Claude's capabilities, develop evals, and design scalable architectures that maximize the value of our AI systems. Responsibilities: Partner with account executives to deeply understand customer requirements and translate them into technical solutions, ensuring alignment between business objectives and technical implementation Serve as the primary technical advisor to enterprise customers throughout their Claude adoption journey, from discovery to initial evaluation through deployment. You will need to coordinate internally across multiple teams & stakeholders to drive customer success Support customers building with both the Claude API and Claude for Work Create and deliver compelling technical content tailored to different audiences. You will need to be able to spread the gamut from technical deep dives for engineering & development teams up to business value focused conversations with executives Guide technical architecture decisions and help customers integrate Claude effectively into their existing technology stack Help customers develop evaluation frameworks to measure Claude's performance for their specific use cases Identify common integration patterns and contribute insights back to our Product and Engineering teams Travel occasionally to customer sites for workshops, technical deep dives, and relationship building Maintain strong knowledge of the latest developments in LLM capabilities and implementation patterns You may be a good fit if you have: 5+ years of experience in technical customer-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, or Technical Account Manager Experience working with enterprise customers, navigating complex buying cycles involving multiple stakeholders Exceptional ability to build relationships with and communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders to include C-suite executives, engineering & IT teams, and more Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate customer requirements between technical and business stakeholders Experience designing scalable cloud architectures and integrating with enterprise systems Comfortable with python Familiarity with common LLM frameworks and tools or a background in machine learning or data science Excitement for engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities A love of teaching, mentoring, and helping others succeed Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to convey complicated topics in easily understandable terms to a diverse set of external and internal stakeholders. You enjoy engaging in cross-organizational collaboration, working through trade-offs, and balancing competing priorities Passion for thinking creatively about how to use technology in a way that is safe and beneficial, and ultimately furthers the goal of advancing safe AI systems Deadline to apply:  None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.  The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.  For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: £165,000 — £190,000 GBP Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage:  Learn about  our policy for using AI in our application process.

Vous vous intégrez aux équipes techniques de GSI et des partenaires cloud pour mettre en œuvre leurs pratiques en matière d'IA, vous aider à résoudre les problèmes, promouvoir Anthropic au sein de leurs communautés de développeurs et servir de point d'accès pour les problèmes techniques complexes. jobs.title: Applied AI Demo Engineer
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's customer-facing teams are often the first place a customer sees what Claude can do. As a Demo Engineer, you'll build the demos, reference implementations, and reusable tooling that help those teams make new capabilities tangible, relevant, and trustworthy, ideally within days of a product launch rather than weeks after. This role sits between product engineering, technical storytelling, and GTM execution. You'll own ambiguous, high-leverage problems end to end: prototyping an agentic experience for a new capability, then hardening it into something reliable that other teams can run on their own. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, and our sales and solutions teams, and you'll bring what you learn from customer-facing work back to the people building the products. Because a demo is frequently someone's first impression of what our models can and can't do, accuracy and honesty matter as much as polish. Success in this role looks like customer-facing teams demonstrating new capabilities sooner and with more confidence, recurring requests becoming reusable assets rather than one-off projects, and field insights shaping product and launch-readiness decisions. jobs.title: Business Systems Analyst, GTM Systems
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's go-to-market engine runs on Salesforce: how leads become pipeline, how deals are tracked and forecast, how customers renew and expand, and how partners work alongside our sellers. As a Business Systems Analyst, you'll be responsible for how one of those core motions is represented in system, and a trusted partner to GTM leadership when they want to change how it works. We're looking for someone who operates at the intersection of three things: a strategist who can sit with GTM leaders and shape how they want to understand their part of the business, an analyst who can turn that into rigorous process and data design, and a builder who's comfortable enough in Salesforce to ship meaningful parts of it themselves. You can move fluidly between whiteboard, requirements doc, and admin console. You'll partner deeply with RevOps on the operating model and with our Salesforce developers on anything that needs code. Where you might sit We're hiring across several parts of the customer lifecycle. Placement depends on your background and where you can have the most impact. Opportunity Acceleration: Owns how deals are tracked, forecast, and credited in Salesforce, from stage design and forecasting to the ownership and team structures behind them. You'll partner with sales leadership to make pipeline something everyone can trust and sellers can work quickly. Lead-to-Pipeline: Owns how leads, inbound demand, and BDR outreach become qualified pipeline: lifecycle stages, routing and ownership, handoff rules, and the tools BDRs and sellers work in every day. You'll partner with BDR, marketing, and sales leadership to make the path from first touch to open opportunity faster and easier to measure. Post-Sales: Owns the systems behind renewals, expansion, and customer coverage: how post-sale opportunities are created, forecast, and worked by account management and customer success. Deployment runs from construction kickoff to ready for service (RFS). You are engaged during planning and construction, and on-site and hands-on from EFA through infrastructure delivery and receiving, integration QA, power-on and network turn-up, burn-in and validation, and acceptance. jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Compute Infrastructure
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large-scale compute clusters that serve the models backing ChatGPT and the API, while also supporting training workloads for our next generation of models. We provide a unified platform for OpenAI teams to run production Applied AI and Research training workloads. Our work spans cloud providers, bare metal infrastructure, data centers, and the foundational services that make compute usable. We partner across Engineering, Research, Product, Capacity Planning, Finance, and Data Center Infrastructure to bring new capacity online and support OpenAI’s growing compute needs. We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Technical Program Manager for Compute Infrastructure, you will own the supply signal for all GPUs entering our fleet: a reliable view of what capacity is arriving, where and when it will arrive, and when it is expected to become usable. You will own the roadmap, requirements, delivery, and adoption of the tools, data, and platform behind that signal, partnering with Engineering to build systems that support planning and execution across OpenAI. You will also lead programs that turn incoming supply into usable compute. Working across cloud providers, Data Center Infrastructure, and compute engineering teams, you will connect physical site readiness with the CPU, storage, network, GPU, and foundational services required to bring new sites and clusters online. You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, managing a broad portfolio of infrastructure programs and making dependencies, risks, and decisions clear from working teams through leadership. Your work will help teams plan with confidence, respond to supply changes, and deliver capacity on time. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Own the GPU supply signal across the fleet. Maintain a trusted view of incoming capacity across providers, sites, and clusters, including quantities, delivery forecasts, acceptance and readiness milestones, and expected dates for production use. Make changes and their downstream effects visible. - Build and scale the tools, data, and platform behind that signal. Own the roadmap, requirements, delivery, and adoption, partnering with Engineering on data models, integrations, quality checks, and planning workflows. Serve Product TPMs, Capacity TPMs, and Compute TPMs, alongside Finance, Accounting, leadership, Engineering, and Research. - Connect supply with capacity planning. Partner with Capacity Planning on supply and demand management, allocation planning, and scenario analysis. Ensure plans reflect current supply forecasts, infrastructure constraints, and the effects of early or late deliveries. - Coordinate physical readiness for new capacity. Work closely with Data Center Infrastructure and cloud service providers to align ready-for-service dates, site construction, power and cooling readiness, supply-chain convergence, equipment delivery, and commissioning. Track dependencies and drive resolution of gaps that threaten deployment. - Lead logical readiness across infrastructure resources. Coordinate CPU, storage, network, GPU, Kubernetes, and dependent compute foundation services so new clusters can support their intended workloads. Make clear which missing services or resources could delay GPU use. - Drive deployment across cloud and bare metal environments. Lead integrated plans across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other infrastructure partners, accounting for provider-specific dependencies while establishing consistent readiness criteria and handoffs. - Establish Delivery Scorecards for cloud providers and internal infrastructure teams. Track delivery commitments, forecast changes, actual delivery, readiness milestones, and time to usable capacity. Use these scorecards to identify recurring gaps, clarify recovery actions, and improve delivery predictability. - Improve the reliability and repeatability of cluster bringup. Partner with Engineering to scale automation, runbooks, validation, and deployment processes. Reduce manual coordination and the time between capacity delivery and production use. - Manage the critical paths across concurrent programs. Establish clear milestones, owners, dependencies, and escalation paths. Resolve cross-team blockers and drive decisions that keep site and cluster deployments moving. - Communicate progress, risks, and tradeoffs clearly. Give technical and business stakeholders the information they need to understand capacity availability, assess changes to the plan, and make timely decisions. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have 5+ years of experience leading major technical programs, including compute infrastructure, hyperscaler deployments, capital projects, or similarly complex infrastructure work. - Possess a degree in a hard science or engineering discipline, or have a demonstrated track record of equivalent engineering expertise. - Are familiar with Kubernetes deployments and have worked with at least one major cloud provider—such as AWS, GCP, Azure, or OCI—to scale compute infrastructure. Experience coordinating deployments across multiple providers is valuable. - Are familiar with bare metal GPU capacity and the provisioning, inventory, and planning systems used to bring it into service. - Have worked with Capacity Planning teams on supply and demand management, allocations, constraints, and supporting tools. You understand how changes in delivery or readiness affect downstream capacity plans. - Have experience defining requirements for operational data and internal platforms. You can work with engineers to establish useful data models, improve data quality, and build tools that teams adopt and rely on. - Understand how site readiness, power and cooling, equipment delivery, commissioning, and ready-for-service milestones affect cluster deployment. You can coordinate these dependencies without losing sight of when the intended workload can run. - Have a record of owning and delivering complex technical programs across internal teams and external partners, including cloud providers, equipment suppliers, or data center infrastructure teams. - Are technically adept and comfortable working with Engineering and Research to understand dependencies, evaluate tradeoffs, and turn complex problems into executable plans. - Build simple, scalable processes and communicate clearly with both technical teams and business stakeholders. You are resourceful in ambiguous environments and follow issues through to resolution. - Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates.
